candidates.name: Diyala Gas Fields Supply Pipeline (Gilabat-Qumar / Khashim Ahmer-Injana to Diyala power plants)
aka: Crescent Petroleum Diyala gas project pipelines
candidates.sponsor: Crescent Petroleum (20-year contracts with Ministry of Oil / Midland Oil Company)
candidates.from: Gilabat-Qumar and Khashim Ahmer-Injana gas fields, Diyala Governorate
candidates.to: Nearby power plants in Diyala (press reports name the Mansuriyah power plant as a primary offtaker)

evidence.note: Crescent press release on signing three 20-year contracts: Diyala fields to initially produce 250 MMscfd of gas; 'The company will build a processing plant on site as well as pipelines and infrastructure to supply gas'; first gas expected within 18 months to supply nearby power plants.
Same press release via Zawya, independently confirming the pipelines-and-infrastructure scope for supplying Diyala power plants from Gilabat-Qumar and Khashim Ahmer-Injana.
Crescent completed first phase of 3D seismic at Khashim al Ahmer (Diyala) in April 2025 — project active but still in appraisal, so the supply pipeline is most likely still pre-construction.

candidates.why_maybe_new: No roster row covers a new-build line from the Gilabat-Qumar / Khashim Ahmer-Injana fields to Diyala power plants. Closest possible confusions: P4058 Eastern Iraq Gas Pipeline (48in, endpoints unknown in roster — believed to be the existing Iranian-import corridor feeding Diyala/Baghdad plants, not this new-build) and the Mansuriya FIELD itself (Sinopec development collapsed; no GEM pipeline row exists for it). Volume ramps from ~120-250 MMscfd initially toward ~520 MMscfd to Mansuriyah and nearby plants per trade press, which puts it at transmission scale rather than in-field gathering. Consolidator should confirm it is not treated as part of the plant/field boundary.

candidates.name: Kurdistan-Turkey Gas Export Pipeline (Rosneft-KRG)
aka: KRG gas export pipeline to Turkey
candidates.sponsor: Rosneft (BOOT arrangement) with Kurdistan Regional Government Ministry of Natural Resources
candidates.from: Kurdistan Region gas fields (Khor Mor area / KRI network)
candidates.to: Turkish border, for export to Turkey and onward to Europe

evidence.note: Rosneft press release (18 Sep 2017): agreement to fund and build a gas pipeline in Iraqi Kurdistan handling up to 30 bcm/yr for export plus domestic supply to KRI power plants and industry; BOOT structure; domestic supply from 2019, exports from 2020.
Washington Institute analysis: Rosneft agreed to construct a 30 bcm/yr gas pipeline to Turkey (deal signed at St. Petersburg forum); project still in development phase, never reached construction.

candidates.why_maybe_new: No roster row matches a KRG-to-Turkey gas export line. It is distinct from P7573 Basra-Ceyhan Gas Pipeline (federal Iraq proposal, southern route) and from the domestic KRI lines P4047 Khormor-Erbil, P4053 Erbil-Duhok and P7457 Semel-Duhok, which stop well short of the border. The original 2019/2020 timeline lapsed and Rosneft partially divested from Kurdish midstream, so shelved (possibly cancelled) is the right bucket; GEM may want it for historical/announced coverage. Borderline risk: if GEM considers P4053 Erbil-Duhok (52in per roster) the first leg of this export scheme, the consolidator should merge rather than add.
